summary: Iteration 110 — Admin orders now surface the owning manager, a manager can no longer set client conditions directly (only request-and-approve), a monthly sales chart was added on /admin/staff, and manager commission payouts are tracked. Fully covered end-to-end. Backend: new file test_iter110_mgr_orders_payouts_chart.py 14/14 pass; iter109 regression file updated (removed tests of the removed direct PUT endpoint, added tests for the 404/405 of the old endpoint and validation of the new POST /manager/clients/{id}/conditions-request) and 25/25 still pass. Covered: (1) MANAGER REQUESTS — PUT /manager/clients/{id}/conditions returns 404/405; POST /manager/clients/{id}/conditions-request creates a pending request (manager-only, 404 for foreign client, validation 422 on negative discount/delivery/credit and discount>100, 400 on second pending for same client, admin sees manager_id/manager_name in GET /admin/conditions-requests); client's conditions and customer_status remain UNCHANGED until approval (verified via /my-conditions and /cart/preview); /my-conditions.pending_request is null for a manager-originated request; admin approve applies the ADMIN's values (even when different from what the manager requested) and keeps customer_status=retail (manager-originated); admin reject changes nothing; a client's OWN approved request still flips him to wholesale. (2) ADMIN ORDERS — GET /api/admin/orders items include manager_name for orders of bound clients; orders of unbound clients have manager_name falsy; UI badge order-manager-{orderId} 'Менеджер: <name>' renders (145 badges on live admin orders page, first text 'Менеджер: TEST_StatMgr'). (3) PAYOUTS — GET /api/admin/staff/{id}/payouts returns {earned, paid, balance, payouts[]} with earned = profit*commission_percent (10% here → >0 after test order); POST validates amount>0 (0 and −10 → 422), bad date → 400, unknown manager → 404; successful create with custom paid_at and default today both work; GET /admin/staff rows include a payouts object; DELETE soft-cancels (payout disappears, balance restored) and second DELETE → 404; demo-client gets 403 on admin payouts endpoints, demo-manager 403 on admin create/delete; GET /manager/payouts returns the manager's own summary; admin & client → 403 on /manager/payouts. (4) SALES CHART — GET /api/admin/staff-chart default months=12, each row {month:'YYYY-MM', <managerId>: revenue}; months clamped to 1..36 (0→1, 100→36); non-admin 403; after a TEST_ order against a new TEST_ manager the current-month cell for that manager > 0 and the manager is in the managers[] array. Frontend smoke on the live external URL: admin /admin/staff shows staff-sales-chart with recharts SVG bars and staff-balance-* column; opening a manager renders payouts-panel with payouts-earned / -paid / -balance / payout-amount-input / payout-date / payout-comment-input / payout-add-btn / payouts-list; /admin/staff requests tab lists conditions-request-* cards; /admin/orders shows order-manager-* badges; /manager stats shows manager-payouts-summary with manager-payouts-balance; /manager clients shows manager-edit-conditions-{id} labelled 'Запросить условия у администратора' which opens manager-conditions-modal with mgr-discount/mgr-delivery/mgr-deferral/mgr-credit-limit/mgr-comment and manager-conditions-save 'Отправить запрос'.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/staff.py decide_conditions_request calls _apply_individual_conditions for the manager-originated branch with an empty extra dict — any legacy customer_status on that client is preserved (retail stays retail, which is the intended behaviour here), but delivery_cost/deferral_days/credit_limit are overwritten unconditionally. The UI already sends the full shape, so this is fine, but a partial PUT would silently wipe other individual fields.

routes/staff.py staff_chart iterates orders and bucketises by the first 7 chars of created_at (string compare). Orders created outside the keys window are ignored via the $gte filter — OK. However if an order document stores created_at without a leading ISO date (legacy numeric timestamp etc.) it would miss; safe for current schema but brittle.

routes/staff.py _payout_summary runs _manager_stats(..., 'all', detailed=False) inside list_staff for EVERY manager — N+1 over orders / products / stock_movements. For >20–30 managers this is noticeable. Consider caching the all-time commission per manager or a single aggregation.
routes/staff.py cancel_payout uses a soft-cancel flag — the record stays in Mongo forever. A monthly clean-up of `cancelled_at IS NOT NULL` older than N days would keep the collection small.
routes/staff.py add_payout accepts amount>earned (no cap) — balance can go negative. If a negative balance is undesirable, enforce amount <= balance on creation.

models.py OrderResponse still omits manager_id (see iter109 review note). GET /admin/orders now adds manager_name server-side so the UI works, but third-party / mobile consumers of /orders can't read the manager link.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=$(grep -oP 'REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=\K\S+' /app/frontend/.env) && python -m pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter110_mgr_orders_payouts_chart.py /app/backend/tests/test_iter109_staff_managers.py -p no:xdist -o addopts='' -v`. The manager-originated conditions request intentionally keeps the client at customer_status=retail even after approval (spec); the client's OWN approved request still makes him wholesale. OrderResponse still omits manager_id — read /admin/staff/{id}/stats or /admin/orders (manager_name) to verify order attribution; the order POST response won't show it. payout-date in the UI is a calendar popover button (not a text input) — leave empty or click a day; the backend accepts missing paid_at (default today) and the test uses that pattern. test_iter110 cancels its own order inside the TestPayouts.test_payouts_full_flow — do not depend on commission 10% persisting after this test; subsequent revenue-based checks cancel their own orders in teardown.
